title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) may set with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.
step: With the engine idling, inspect the PCV hose where it joins the intake elbow, flexing it gently while you listen for a vacuum hiss
results: I flexed the PCV hose at the elbow with it idling. No cracks and no hiss.
The PCV hose at the elbow looks fine, and I can't hear any hiss even when I bend it.

title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor, model years 2010-2015. Lean codes with high long-term fuel trim at idle may set when a contaminated sensor element under-reports airflow. With the engine warm and idling and all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement. Do not touch the sensor element. Repair: clean the sensor element or replace the sensor.
step: With the engine warm and idling and the accessories off, read mass airflow on a scan tool and compare it with roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement
results: The scan tool shows the MAF right about where it should be for my engine size at idle.
MAF reading at warm idle matched the 1 g/s per liter rule almost exactly.

title: Long crank on hot restarts from fuel pressure bleed-down
text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2015. Rail pressure that bleeds down lets fuel boil in a hot rail and lengthens hot restarts. Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later. It should stay above 30 psi. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the pump module.
step: Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the fuel rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later; it should still be above 30 psi
results: Put a gauge on after a drive. Still 42 psi after twenty minutes.

title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Overfueling can cause a long crank on hot restarts. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.
step: On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator held to the floor to put the engine in clear-flood mode and note whether it fires noticeably faster
results: Tried it with the pedal floored on a hot restart. Cranked just as long, no difference.
The clear-flood trick made no difference. Still a long crank when it's hot.

title: Long crank on cold starts from overfueling
text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Overfueling can cause a long crank on cold starts. On any cold start, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.

title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.
step: Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling
results: Pulled the plug. Gap is 0.042, no cracks, and it looks like the others.
The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain.

Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.

title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4 and 3.5L V6 engines with electric radiator fans. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic, but not at speed, if the fan does not run. With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.
step: With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool and confirm the fan starts
results: Turned the AC on and the radiator fan kicked on right away.

title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan

title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
text: Applies to gasoline engines, model years 2011-2021. Scale or debris in the radiator core can make temperature climb at idle and in traffic. With the engine warm and the thermostat open, compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank using an infrared thermometer. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: flush or replace the radiator.
step: With the engine at operating temperature, compare the radiator inlet and outlet tank temperatures with an infrared thermometer, sweeping it across the core for cold spots
results: Inlet was 205 and outlet 172, and I didn't find any cold spots on the core.

title: Coolant loss with no visible leak from an early-venting cap
text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. Coolant may drop slowly with no visible leak when the pressure cap vents early and coolant escapes through the overflow as vapor. Fit the cap to a pressure tester adapter and pump until it vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.

results: The cap held its rated 16 psi on the adapter.

title: Weak heat in cold weather from a thermostat stuck open
text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4 and 2.4L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Heater output may be weak, even with a normal temperature gauge, when the thermostat sticks partly open. From a cold start, idle the engine and watch coolant temperature on a scan tool while feeling the upper radiator hose. It should stay cool until about 195 deg F. Repair: replace the thermostat and gasket.

title: Cool vent air from a skipping blend door actuator
text: Applies to model years 2016-2021. Vent air may stay cool when the blend door actuator skips or stops short of full hot. With the engine warm, run the climate control from full cold to full hot while listening behind the center of the dash. The actuator should move smoothly through its full travel. Repair: replace and recalibrate the blend door actuator.

title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2016-2021. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.
step: With the doors closed and the modules asleep, connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal; draw should settle below 50 mA
results: Waited 45 minutes and the draw settled at 28 mA.
Meter read 0.03 amps once everything went to sleep.

title: Dim lights at idle from a slipping accessory belt
text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Lights may dim at idle under load when a glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip. With the engine off, inspect the drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. Repair: replace the belt and tensioner.

title: Flickering lights from a failed alternator diode
text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines. Headlights may flicker or dim at idle because a failed rectifier diode reduces alternator output. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.
step: With the engine at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, measure AC ripple voltage across the battery posts and compare it with 0.5 V AC
results: Ripple was 0.08 volts AC.

title: Click with no crank from the starter control circuit
text: Applies to vehicles with an automatic transmission or CVT, model years 2016-2021. The starter may click or stay silent in park when the range switch, starter relay or wiring drops voltage to the solenoid. Back-probe the solenoid S terminal and have a helper attempt a start in park. The S terminal should see at least 10.5 V during the attempt. Use a back-probe pin so the connector seal is not damaged. Repair: correct the switch, relay or wiring fault.

results: Got 11.8 volts at the S terminal when it clicks.

title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation felt through the steering wheel may develop when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.

title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout

title: Pull during braking from binding caliper slide pins
text: Applies to vehicles with floating front calipers. A pull during braking may come from a corroded or swollen slide pin that binds and causes uneven pad pressure. Remove each front caliper from its bracket without disconnecting the hose, pull each slide pin and check for corrosion, a swollen boot or binding. Pins should move freely by hand. Repair: clean and lubricate the pins, or fit new pins and boots.
step: Remove the front calipers from their brackets and confirm each slide pin moves freely through its full travel without binding
results: Slide pins on both sides slide freely, no rust.

title: Pull while cruising from binding caliper slide pins

title: Brake pull from a restricted front brake hose
text: Applies to midsize sedans and small crossovers, model years 2011-2020. A pull during braking, sometimes with one front wheel running hot, may come from a front brake hose that collapses internally and restricts fluid return. With the front wheels raised, have a helper press and release the pedal firmly. Spin each front wheel by hand right after release; both should turn freely. Repair: replace both front brake hoses.

title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
text: Applies to vehicles with front struts, model years 2010-2022. A worn strut upper mount or bearing can clunk over bumps or when turning slowly. With a helper bouncing the front, rest a hand on the upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop. Repair: replace the upper mounts and bearings.

title: Steering wheel shake at highway speed from wheel imbalance
text: Applies to vehicles from model years 2011-2021. A steering wheel shake that peaks in a narrow band such as 60-70 mph may come from tire and wheel assemblies that are out of balance or have high road-force variation. Check each assembly on a road-force balancer. Imbalance should be under 0.25 oz and road-force variation under about 20 lb. Repair: rebalance the assemblies and match-mount as needed.

results: A shop road-force balanced all four and they were all within spec.

title: Pedal that sinks at a stop from master cylinder bypass
text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans and hatchbacks, model years 2010-2020. Fluid bypassing the master cylinder seals lets the pedal sink slowly at a stop with no external leak. With the engine off, pump the pedal several times to use up booster reserve. Apply steady, moderate pressure and hold it for one minute. Watch the pedal height against a fixed mark. Repair: replace the master cylinder and bleed the system.

title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts that worsen as the fluid warms. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.
